pages.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025 — peripheral immune tolerance

facts.text: Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary E. Brunkow, Frederick J. Ramsdell — for peripheral immune tolerance
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Shimon Sakaguchi (1995); Discovery: Regulatory T cells (T-regs) — CD4⁺CD25⁺ subset in mice
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Brunkow & Ramsdell (2001); Discovery: Gene FOXP3 — mutations cause IPEX syndrome (humans), scurfy (mice)
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: ⚠ Central tolerance = deletion of self-reactive T-cells in thymus; peripheral tolerance works outside thymus
facts.head: Exam angle

facts.text: Applications: autoimmune diseases (type-1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus), transplants, cancer immunotherapy
facts.head: Exam angle

facts.text: Date: 6 October 2025 — 222nd session of UNESCO Executive Board nominated Khaled El-Enany (Egypt)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Defeated: Édouard Firmin Matoko (Republic of Congo)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Final appointment: UNESCO General Conference in Uzbekistan
facts.head: News

facts.text: Profile: Egyptologist; Egypt's Minister of Antiquities (2016–2019), later Tourism and Antiquities; backed by African Union and Arab League
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ Would be the first Arab Director-General
facts.head: News

facts.text: Context: USA withdrew from UNESCO in July 2025
facts.head: News

pages.title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2025 — macroscopic quantum tunnelling

facts.text: John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, John M. Martinis — macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting circuits
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Platform: Josephson junction — two superconductors separated by thin insulator; Cooper pairs
facts.head: Key science

facts.text: Applications: superconducting qubits, circuit QED, quantum amplifiers, sensors
facts.head: Key science

facts.text: Example of tunnelling in nature: nuclear fusion in the Sun
facts.head: Key science

pages.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2025 — Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs)

facts.text: Laureate: Susumu Kitagawa (Japan, Kyoto University); Contribution: Flexible / "soft" MOFs letting gases flow in and out
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Richard Robson (UK/Australia); Contribution: First concept — copper ions with four-armed organic molecules
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Omar M. Yaghi (USA/Jordanian-American, UC Berkeley); Contribution: Highly stable, designable MOFs — water harvesting from desert air, CO₂ capture
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: MOFs: crystalline porous materials of metal ions + organic ligands
facts.head: Exam angle

facts.text: ⚠ Unlike rigid zeolites, some MOFs can "breathe"
facts.head: Exam angle

facts.text: Uses: removing PFAS from water, carbon capture, gas storage, drug delivery, catalysis
facts.head: Exam angle

pages.title: Nobel Prize in Literature 2025 — László Krasznahorkai

facts.text: László Krasznahorkai (Hungary), 71 — "singular prose that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art"

facts.text: Work: War and War; Year: 1999
facts.head: Works

facts.text: Work: Destruction and Sorrow Beneath the Heavens; Year: 2004

pages.title: Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences 2025 — innovation-driven growth

facts.text: Laureate: Joel Mokyr; Country: US-Israel; Contribution: Prerequisites for sustained growth through technological progress (historical analysis)
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Philippe Aghion; Country: France; Contribution: Theory of sustained growth via creative destruction — 1992 model with Howitt
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Laureate: Peter Howitt; Country: Canada; Contribution: Co-developed creative destruction model
facts.head: Winners

facts.text: Creative destruction: coined by Joseph Schumpeter (1942) — "Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy"
facts.head: Background

facts.text: ⚠ Economics prize (Sveriges Riksbank Prize) set up in 1968 by Sweden's central bank — not in Nobel's will
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Prize: gold medal, diploma, $1.2 million
facts.head: Background

facts.text: 2024 winners: Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson
facts.head: Background
